rulings.text: The loan «بٹن» is not written. P16-test (b0-ui) lists it REFUSED, N89 keeps it refused and N730 adds no noun «بٹن»; condition (2) of the test is not met here (no reader read a native form and was misled; the on-05 reader understood the loan), so the judge cannot admit it. As in N89 and N730, the element is named by its own interface label quoted byte for byte in “ ”: the published tmap.locate «نقشے پر دکھائیں» (its tooltip and accessible name), with its position «کسی بھی نام کے ساتھ» kept; the icon’s shape is not described. The verb stays «چن کر»: N332 (E) makes «چنیں» the device-neutral verb for the reader’s action and N730 uses it after a quoted button label; «کلک» and «ٹیپ» are barred by P16 and N332 (B), «دبا کر» by N89, N332 (C) and N727. The reader’s remark that «چن کر» is unusual for clicking is therefore rejected on the line’s rulings. «اسے» becomes «وہ مقام» (reader #5), and «نقشے پر» is not repeated after the label that already says it. Cost, charged under accuracy: the label shows as a tooltip, so on touch the reader finds the element by its position; the fresh readers on final test this. Binds tmap.howto only.

Round 2, on the fresh phone reader of final (06-blind-final.md, 72/100). (A) THE CONTROL. Quoting the label «نقشے پر دکھائیں» is withdrawn: on a phone it is only a tooltip and the reader could not tie it to the icon (P1), the cost round 1 predicted. P16-test re-run for «بٹن» on this evidence: condition (2) is now met (a reader was misled by the native, label-quoting form); condition (3) is met (a dictionary headword); condition (1) is NOT shown: no localized interface or press page was obtained in this pass, and the test asks that the native wording be shown not to be what the thing is called, while what a phone user sees here is a small sign, and Urdu has a common native noun for that, «نشان», already published on the line («تیر کے نشانوں», «علامتی نشان»). The owner’s rule (P16) keeps a loan out where a common native word exists; the loan stays refused. The control is named by its position and as a small sign: «ہر نام کے ساتھ والے چھوٹے سے نشان»; the shape is not described. «ہر نام» replaces «کسی بھی نام» (P3: vague); before/after is not stated because the sources say beside and the layout is not fixed by direction. Cost: on a map page «نشان» can also mean a marker; «فہرست میں ہر نام کے ساتھ» places it in the list. (B) THE VERB, re-weighed after two independent readers (05 #5, final P2/P4) flagged «چن کر» and asked for «ٹیپ کر کے» or «دبا کر». The termbase leaves these native options: «چنیں» (N332 E, N730: device-neutral for acting on a place, an option or a button) and «کھولیں» / «کھول کر» (N720, N89: device-neutral for opening a place or a link). Barred: «کلک», «ٹیپ» (P16, N332 B; P16-test condition (1) not shown for either: 0 pages on ur.wikipedia for «ٹیپ کریں» per N332), «دبا کر» (N89, N332 C, N727: reads as a physical press, refused there on the same reader suggestion), «چھو کر» (N720: touch only). THE NAME is a link that opens a page, so its verb becomes «کھول کر» on the N720 frame «… کو کھول کر … دیکھیں» (published HOME map.lead): this answers P4. THE ICON opens nothing (it moves the map), so «کھول کر» does not fit it (N730’s reason for a button that opens nothing), and «چن کر» is the only admissible native verb left: kept for the icon, with the two readers’ stumble charged under fluency. If the owner wants a loan verb here, that is his decision under P16, raised in one line: «… نشان پر ٹیپ کر کے …». Binds tmap.howto only.
